Forecast Discussion

Instead of being between two ferns, we are between two fronts today. One is stationary to our east and south; the other is approaching from the northwest and will move across the mountains early Friday and then stall briefly nearby.

Thursday is warm and humid with scattered afternoon showers and thunderstorms, especially along the east side of the Appalachians (near the Blue Ridge). Showers and thunderstorms are still around this evening but taper off by midnight. Friday has more clouds and will be slightly less warm with an increase in overall afternoon showers and thunderstorm coverage.

The Friday front will be to our south and east during the weekend with high pressure building in from the northwest. We still have the potential for widely scattered afternoon showers and thunderstorms Saturday (less than Friday) and isolated shower and thundershower coverage Sunday.

Beginning Monday, the Atlantic ridge builds westward, and high pressure will be over the Southeast. Heat and humidity return from the south. Showers and thunderstorms will be more isolated each afternoon, driven by heating of the mountaintops. We will be approaching record highs for the dates by Wednesday and Thursday of next week.
